knowledge_point.title: Integrating Quotients Containing Trigonometric Functions Using Substitution

question.:question/worked-solution:
Let $u=\tan{\left(x \right)} + 1,$ then

$$
\frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}x}=\tan^{2}{\left(x \right)} + 1.
$$

Using the above, we can write the integral in terms of $u$ and evaluate:

$$
\begin{aligned}\int \left(1 - \frac{1}{\tan{\left(x \right)} + 1}\right) \left(9 \tan^{2}{\left(x \right)} + 9\right)\,\text{d}x &= 9\int 1 - \frac{1}{u}\,\text{d}u \\ &= -9\ln|u|+9 u+C \\ &= 9-9\ln|\tan{\left(x \right)} + 1|+9 \tan{\left(x \right)}+C\end{aligned}
$$

question.:question/worked-solution:
Let $u=\sin{\left(x^{2} \right)},$ then

$$
\frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}x}=2 x \cos{\left(x^{2} \right)}.
$$

Using the above, we can write the integral in terms of $u$ and evaluate:

$$
\begin{aligned}\int \frac{6 x \cos{\left(x^{2} \right)}}{\sin{\left(x^{2} \right)}}\,\text{d}x &= 3\int \frac{1}{u}\,\text{d}u \\ &= 3\ln|u|+C \\ &= 3\ln|\sin{\left(x^{2} \right)}|+C\end{aligned}
$$

question.:question/worked-solution:
Let $u=8 \cos^{3}{\left(x \right)} + 5,$ then

$$
\frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}x}=- 24 \sin{\left(x \right)} \cos^{2}{\left(x \right)}.
$$

Calculating the limits for $u$ gives

| $x$ | $\frac{\pi}{3}$ | $\frac{\pi}{2}$ |
| --- | --- | --- |
| $u$ | $6$ | $5$ |

Using the above, we can write the integral in terms of $u$ and evaluate:

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{\frac{\pi}{3}}^{\frac{\pi}{2}}\frac{216 \sin{\left(x \right)} \cos^{2}{\left(x \right)}}{8 \cos^{3}{\left(x \right)} + 5}\,\text{d}x &= -9{\int }_{6}^{5}\frac{1}{u}\,\text{d}u \\ &= - 9 \ln{\left(u \right)}\big|_{6}^{5} \\ &= - 9 \ln{\left(5 \right)}-(- 9 \ln{\left(6 \right)}) \\ &= \ln{\left(\frac{10077696}{1953125} \right)}\end{aligned}
$$

question.:question/worked-solution:
Let $u=\csc{\left(x \right)} + 2,$ then

$$
\frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}x}=- \cot{\left(x \right)} \csc{\left(x \right)}.
$$

Using the above, we can write the integral in terms of $u$ and evaluate:

$$
\begin{aligned}\int \frac{18 \cot{\left(x \right)} \csc{\left(x \right)}}{\csc{\left(x \right)} + 2}\,\text{d}x &= -18\int \frac{1}{u}\,\text{d}u \\ &= -18\ln|u|+C \\ &= -18\ln|\csc{\left(x \right)} + 2|+C\end{aligned}
$$
